tasks.prompt: Model the car's charging subsystem in the logical architecture (LA): the functions and components involved in charging the accumulator, how they connect to the rest of the car, and the limits that apply.
brief: The charger is an off-board commercial unit that stays in the paddock; no part of it is mounted on the car.
The charger and the BMS talk over CAN: the BMS sends the current and voltage setpoints and can tell the charger to stop.
The maximum charge current is 15 A.
Charging stops when any cell reaches 4.15 V.
Charging also stops when any cell temperature exceeds 45 °C.
The charging shutdown circuit runs through an HVIL loop in the charging connector: unplugging the connector opens it.

tasks.prompt: Model the cooling of the tractive system in the logical architecture (LA): what is cooled, how heat is moved and rejected, and the temperature limits that apply.
brief: Motor and inverter share one liquid loop; the coolant is plain water.
There is a single radiator, in the left sidepod.
The radiator fan switches on above 40 °C coolant temperature.
The inverter derates torque when its coolant inlet exceeds 50 °C.
The motor derates when its winding temperature reaches 120 °C.
The accumulator is not on the water loop: it is air-cooled by two fans pulling air through the segments.

The inverter is a Cascadia PM100.
The VCU sends the torque request to the inverter over CAN every 10 ms.
The torque request is capped at 180 N·m at the motor.

tasks.prompt: Model how the team charges the accumulator at competition, in the operational analysis (OA): who takes part, what each of them does, and where.
brief: Charging happens only in the charging area of the paddock.
The accumulator is taken out of the car and charged on the team's charging cart.
Only the ESO starts charging, with a key switch on the charging cart.
A second team member stands fire watch for the whole charge.
The ESO keeps a charging log, signed at the start and the end of each charge.
